doc.title: Charles Lloyd — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Stevens on Bartok, folk song and Fibonacci
summary: Stevens tells Lloyd that Bartok's folk-song approach matches his own and that Bartok used Fibonacci numbers.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: And so, Halsey saw that I wasn’t gonna work out in missionary position, which is what they had set up.

So he would have me up to his studio and stuff, and talk to me. He told me, he said, “What you like and what’s going on...” Aww man, it almost makes me cry, man. He said, “Bartok is dealing with his folk song, and that’s what you’re dealing with!”
He said, “...and he studied these Fibonacci numbers which came from your country, your people over there in Africa.”
Oh I know you are, I know you are.

But my point is that the school didn’t understand, and Halsey Steven does, and he was also big in Ukrainian songs and stuff like that, and the Russian stuff. But he told me that Bartok was using his folk themes even before I knew - But I mean, Booker and I had heard something in there.
